title: The Glass Orchard (memory trial)
about: Original test story with no private data. Five characters, one central secret, six locations, a death, a promise and a betrayal. Each turn lists what a correct memory should contain afterwards.

story.setting: Brannock Manor sits above a dying orchard of glass-bark trees on a river delta. Lady Orla Brannock is gravely ill. Her steward, Corwin Hale, runs the estate. The player is Ilse Varn, newly hired as the steward's apprentice. Places: the manor hall, the orchard, the chapel, the river docks, the wine cellar, and Lady Orla's bedchamber.
story.lore: Corwin secretly sold the estate's water rights to the smuggler Vey Calder; the orchard is dying because of it. At the start only Corwin and Vey know this. Tamsin Reed is the healer. Brother Aled keeps the chapel and its records.

entries.t: Steward of Brannock Manor, fifties, precise and courteous; hides that he sold the water rights to Vey.
Healer tending Lady Orla; blunt, observant, distrusts Corwin.
Elderly chapel keeper who keeps the estate's sealed records; gentle, fearful.
River smuggler who bought the water rights from Corwin; charming and dangerous.
Owner of the manor, bedridden and failing.

player.name: Ilse Varn
player.desc: The steward's new apprentice, sharp-eyed and careful.

turns.a: I arrive in the manor hall and introduce myself to Corwin Hale.
I ask Corwin to walk me through the orchard and explain why the trees are dying.
I kneel and check the soil by the dry irrigation channels.
I go to Lady Orla's bedchamber, where Tamsin is tending her.
I quietly ask Tamsin what she thinks of Corwin.
I promise Tamsin I will find out why the orchard is dying.
I walk down to the chapel to meet Brother Aled.
I ask Aled to show me the estate's sealed records.
I read the records closely, looking for anything about the river or the water.
I find a deed of sale signed by Corwin that sells the water rights to Vey Calder. I keep my face calm.
I copy the deed by hand and slip the copy into my coat without Aled seeing.
I go back to the manor hall for supper with Corwin and say nothing about the deed.
After supper I go down to the wine cellar alone.
In the cellar I find crates stamped with Vey Calder's mark.
Tamsin finds me in the cellar. I show her the copied deed and tell her Corwin sold the water rights to Vey.
We agree to keep this between us for now.
At dawn I ride to the river docks to find Vey Calder.
I find Vey on his barge and ask him about the water rights without saying how I know.
Vey laughs and warns me to stay out of Corwin's business.
I head back to the manor hall.
I check on Lady Orla in her bedchamber.
Tamsin tells me Orla took a turn for the worse in the night.
I sit with Orla through the evening.
Lady Orla dies in her sleep before dawn.
Corwin gathers the household in the manor hall to announce Orla's death.
Corwin announces that he will manage the estate until an heir is found.
Brother Aled holds a vigil for Orla in the chapel.
After the vigil I take Aled aside and tell him about the deed and the water rights.
Aled is frightened but promises to keep the original deed hidden.
I return to the orchard at night to think.
Corwin finds me in the orchard and asks where I went at dawn.
I lie and tell Corwin I went to buy medicine for Orla.
Corwin doesn't believe me. He orders me to stay inside the manor.
I slip out to the docks anyway to confront Vey.
I show Vey the copied deed and threaten to take it to the magistrate.
Vey offers to betray Corwin in exchange for keeping his barge.
I accept Vey's deal and we shake on it.
I return to the manor hall where Corwin is waiting.
Tamsin and Aled join me as I confront Corwin with the deed.
Corwin confesses that he sold the water rights to pay his debts.
